clue.text: Shop said to have cooler stock

indicators.note: said signals that the words before the name are heard, not spelt, matching it by ear

parts.note: a shop whose stock is coolers would sell fridges

explanation.surface: A shop is rumoured to be holding a cooler range of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: SELFRIDGES is a famous London department store on Oxford Street; spoken, it sounds like 'sell fridges', which is what a shop with cooler stock does.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfridges is a well-known department store, an example of a shop.

clue.text: See 1
River where people act as targets for local guided missiles?

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
the boards is a term for the stage, where actors perform

explanation.surface: A river spot where people stand in as targets for missiles guided locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' means the pub, and its 'guided missiles' are darts, thrown by hand at a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartboards hang in British pubs as targets for thrown darts, playfully called guided missiles.

clue.text: Go mad, getting sectioned

parts.note: to go is to leave or set off
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy and is committed to a psychiatric ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sectioned' suggests being detained under the Mental Health Act, as the British say; here it means split into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Something departmental is divided into departments, that is, organised in sections.

clue.text: Choke or accelerator?

definitions.meaning: to strangle someone by the throat
the valve controlling fuel flow in an engine, opened to speed up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to strangle and the engine control a driver opens to go faster.

clue.text: Character in bar, lowering the tone

definitions.text: Character in bar, lowering the tone

parts.words: Character in bar, lowering the tone
parts.note: read musically: a symbol written in a bar of music that drops a note by a semitone

explanation.surface: Some figure in a pub drags the conversation down.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical notation this sign lowers the pitch of a note by a semitone.

clue.text: Complaint that is put before right Vegas employee?

indicators.note: put before places the preceding letters in front of the following one

parts.note: croup is a childhood illness, a complaint
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Las Vegas worker whose ailment comes before doing the right thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gaming table in a casino, typical of Las Vegas.

clue.text: Book the smallest room

definitions.meaning: one of the four Gospels in the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: John is a Gospel in the Bible and also slang for a toilet.

clue.text: Shortly to be found in pub, Essex girl with two others similarly named

definitions.text: Shortly to be found in pub, Essex
definitions.meaning: a short form of the name, BESS, sits inside the words pub, Essex

definitions.text: girl with two others similarly named
definitions.meaning: a girl's name that splits into two more girls' names, Eliza and Beth

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves point at the same name by different routes; Elizabeth I's favourite was the Earl of Essex, so she was an Essex girl too, and an 'Essex girl' is a British stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name contains the shorter names Eliza and Beth, and Bess is its pet form.

clue.text: Moving slowly round after big end gone

indicators.note: after places the round letter behind the shortened word
end gone says the final letter of the word for big is dropped

parts.note: large means big
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A car crawling around after its big end has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'big end' is part of a car engine whose failure is a notorious breakdown; here it is the end of 'big'.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical tempo marking meaning slow and broad.

clue.text: Setter separates three neighbours from 26 starting to quarrel

indicators.note: separates means the setter's letter splits the run of neighbouring letters

parts.note: three consecutive letters from the 26-letter alphabet
the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: starting takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The setter keeps three neighbours from the 26 apart as they begin to quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' looks like a cross-reference to 26 across, but it means the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Military command given on the go

parts.note: about can mean on, concerning
a turn is a go, as in 'whose go is it?'

explanation.surface: A parade-ground order issued while on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: About turn is the drill order to face the opposite way.

clue.text: Find import of American food item reduced in store, 60% off

indicators.note: in places the American abbreviation and cut soup inside the shortened store
60% off drops three of the five letters of store, keeping its opening two
reduced cuts the last letter from the food item

parts.note: soup is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone discovering an imported American foodstuff on sale cheaply in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss out something is to work out its meaning, its import.

clue.text: Burns house — arson, essentially

indicators.note: essentially means in the middle of these words, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A house burns down, and arson is at the heart of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sears means burns or scorches the surface of something.

clue.text: Model ordered ravioli, forgetting love of trifles

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car

indicators.note: ordered means the remaining letters are arranged anew
forgetting means the letter for love is left out of ravioli

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A model ordered ravioli but forgot she loves trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a food order.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means concerning trifles, things of no importance.

clue.text: Hector, one new boy I see regularly?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Tim is a boy's name
to date someone is to see them regularly

explanation.surface: A new boy at school, possibly one being bullied.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or intimidate.

clue.text: Top part of Western Isle, roughly

definitions.text: Top part of Western Isle, roughly

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are put in a loose new order
top part takes the first letter of the word Western

explanation.surface: Describing the northern area of an island in Scotland's west.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Lewis is the northern part of Lewis and Harris in the Outer Hebrides, the Western Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is the northern section of the island of Lewis and Harris.

clue.text: Girl that's ready to go?

definitions.meaning: the traffic light colour that tells drivers to prepare to move

explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a female name and the traffic light signal shown between red and green in Britain.

clue.text: Retailer flourishing with dodgy deals

parts.note: blooming means flourishing

indicators.note: dodgy means the letters are not as they should be, rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop doing well by doing shady business.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomingdale's is a New York department store chain, a retailer.

clue.text: Provider of venison, eggs and bread in New York

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
bread is money, and buck is American slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A shop list: deer meat, eggs and bread bought in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is a male roe deer, a source of venison.

clue.text: Trustworthy or slippery eel, Blair?

indicators.note: slippery means the letters slide into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether Tony Blair is to be trusted or as slippery as an eel.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliable means dependable, able to be trusted.

clue.text: Connected on the phone, say, then had a fling?

indicators.note: say signals that the phone phrase's word is matched by its sound

parts.note: an operator says you are through when a call is connected

explanation.surface: Someone got through on the phone and then had an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a fling' suggests an affair; it means threw.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw, so had a fling means threw.

clue.text: SOS — Paul's upset regarding marriage

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is dropped, leaving the name

explanation.surface: A distress call from an upset Paul about his marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spousal means relating to a spouse, hence to marriage.

clue.text: Those "in the club" married by end of month, before first sign of shotgun

parts.note: September, November and December all end in these letters

indicators.note: first sign takes only the opening letter of shotgun

explanation.surface: Pregnant women married off at month's end, ahead of a shotgun wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, and a shotgun wedding is a hurried one; here it means belonging to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are the people who belong to a club.

clue.text: See 4
Oddly enough, each loaf I try it's been long in the oven

definitions.text: it's been long in the oven

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third, fifth letters onwards are kept

explanation.surface: A baker remarks that each loaf they try seems to have been baking too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the pastry's shape: it is long, yet does not last long once served, and it is baked in an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a long finger of choux pastry baked in the oven.

clue.text: Fool busy barman with lie

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters bustling into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool of a busy barman telling a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamebrain is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Girl seen in mirror, topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for mirror is removed

parts.note: a glass is a mirror

explanation.surface: A girl seen without her top in the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a northern British and Scots word for a girl.

clue.text: See 19 across
See 18
Yes, he does feature in one setting here

indicators.note: feature in means the letters appear within these words

explanation.surface: Someone confirming that he appears in a setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is a setter for this newspaper, so 'one setting here' means one who sets crosswords here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed is the pseudonym of a crossword setter in this paper.

clue.text: Hedgehog travelling ultra fast

definitions.meaning: the video game hedgehog character from Sega
moving at about the speed of sound

explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog is a game character, and sonic speed is the speed of sound.

clue.text: Ale's drunk before stew is cooked in the US, however

indicators.note: before places the first anagram ahead of the second
drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: read as ale plus s, using all four letters

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up as in a recipe

explanation.surface: Instructions for drinking ale before cooking a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an American variant of at least, meaning anyway or however.
